acr.title: Container Registry
acr.summary: Vyomi's own registry core serves the OCI/Docker Registry v2 push and pull API and ACR extensions from its persisted store; registry:2 is not used for Azure.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.ContainerRegistry registries, tasks, tokens, scope maps, replications, webhooks)
OCI / Docker Registry HTTP API v2 (docker push/pull, oras, crane)
ACR REST extension /acr/v1

offline.notes: Manifests and blobs live in Vyomi's persisted ACR store (AppStateAcrStore), not in a registry:2 container (that container, vyomi-registry, serves Artifact Registry on GCP). ACR Tasks scheduleRun builds through the shared CI seam: real BuildKit offline with --pull=false (only base images already on the host), Gitea as git host only when VYOMI_CI_GITEA=1.

nano.notes: Same registry core in the page for push/pull with digest verification. Builds fall back to a package builder that validates the tree and runs no container, so image build jobs fail with that reason rather than faking success.

differs: Registry credentials, tokens and scope maps are stored and validated but never checked on the data plane: docker/oras can push and pull without presenting them
All registries share one repository store; repositories are not scoped to a login server
Webhooks round-trip but never fire; Event Grid system topics do not receive push/delete events
Geo-replication, cache rules and connected registries are Premium-gated ARM records with no replication or upstream fetch
Imports work only from images already inside Vyomi; Docker Hub, MCR and GHCR sources are refused (no internet egress)
Untagged-manifest retention is enforced when the data plane is called, not by a background job
az acr import is not supported; the import action is carried on /acr/v1/_import
notInScope: Microsoft's global registry network and geo-distribution

aks.title: Azure Kubernetes Service
aks.summary: Vyomi's ARM core stores AKS clusters; on the offline appliance with the k3s backend switched on, each cluster is a real k3s Kubernetes control plane and agents in Docker containers.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.ContainerService managedClusters, agentPools, runCommand, listClusterUserCredential)
kubectl against the real k3s API server using the returned kubeconfig (offline k3s only)
Flux GitOps and Dapr/Keda add-on objects via ARM

offline.notes: Real k3s is opt-in: it runs only when VYOMI_K8S_BACKEND=k3s is set and Docker is reachable. Then node pools become k3s agent containers, stop/start stop the containers, and runCommand/kubeconfig hit the real API server. Without it (or without Docker) the cluster is a simulated object store with no scheduling. The managed Kubernetes category is gated to Pro, Max and Enterprise tiers.

nano.notes: Clusters are stored objects: kubectl apply/get/describe/delete work against the stored manifests through Run command, nothing is scheduled and no pods run. The registry lists Nano as a locked tier for the Kubernetes category (403 FeatureNotAvailableForTier); whether a given Nano session unlocks it was not verified.

differs: Without the k3s backend there is no API server, kubelet or container: controllers create no pods, workloads report 0 ready, the kubeconfig carries placeholder credentials and accepts no kubectl connections
With k3s, Kubernetes versions map to the nearest supported k3s minor (AKS 1.29 to 1.32); the version that really runs is reported as actualVersion
A Kubernetes version upgrade replaces the server and agent containers, not Azure's node image rollout; node pools are containers, not VM scale sets
networkProfile (CNI, network policy, CIDRs) and authorizedIPRanges are validated and stored but not enforced (config only)
StorageClasses map to local-path volumes, not Azure Disk or Files

KEDA, Dapr, Flux and Defender add-ons install their objects; Container Insights and Managed Prometheus create the linked ARM resources without an in-cluster agent shipping telemetry (not verified as shipping)
AKS backup is ARM resources only; no volume snapshot is taken
Cloud identity to Kubernetes RBAC mapping (Entra groups) is not built; workload identity issuer and JWKS are served from the real cluster keys
notInScope: Azure-managed control plane SLA and node image pipeline
Container Insights agent and managed Prometheus collection in the cluster

apim.title: API Management
apim.summary: Vyomi's own gateway core routes requests to APIs and operations, checks subscription keys and runs a subset of policies; the management plane is ARM records.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.ApiManagement service, apis, operations, products, subscriptions, policies, backends, gateways)
Gateway at /azure-data/apim/{service}/{api-path}/{operation} (Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key)

offline.notes: The gateway does longest-prefix API routing, operation matching, subscription-key checks, rate limits and policy execution over the stored records, forwarding to the configured backend URL.

nano.notes: Same gateway in the page. Policies, mock-response, return-response and rejections work; forwarding to a real backend URL is limited by browser network access.

differs: Only a subset of policies is executed; validate-jwt verifies HS256 signatures only and RS256/ES256 are claims-checked with an x-vyomi-apim-warning header; no response caching
Subscription keys are simulator tokens, not signing keys; developer portal CMS and self-service sign-up are not rendered
The real https://{service}.azure-api.net host is not bound; the gateway is path-based
Capacity and Analytics are computed from recorded requests against a nominal requests per second per unit, not CPU or memory
Diagnostic settings and loggers are stored; no telemetry is delivered to Application Insights or Event Hub
Scale-tier limits are enforced only for Consumption and Developer; VNet connectivity, custom-domain TLS and self-hosted gateway connections are ARM configuration only
MCP servers are modelled as APIs of type mcp; the Model Context Protocol surface itself is not served

appconfiguration.title: App Configuration
appconfiguration.summary: Vyomi's own App Configuration core serves key-values, labels, feature flags and snapshots over the azconfig data-plane wire next to the ARM control plane.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.AppConfiguration configurationStores, replicas, keys)
App Configuration data plane (/kv, HMAC or Entra auth)

offline.notes: Key-values live in the ARM state of the store, persisted per space.

nano.notes: Same core in the page.

differs: Feature flags are the standard key convention over key-values, not a separate engine
Replicas are ARM child resources with their own endpoint but reads and writes are not modelled separately; there is one data set
publicNetworkAccess=Disabled returns 403 on the data plane; there is no private network path
Import/export supports JSON, .properties and simple YAML; Key Vault references are copied as plain values
Customer-managed-key encryption is envelope encryption through Vyomi's Key Vault core with a keystream-XOR plus HMAC-SHA256 cipher (core/azure_cmk_core.py), not an AES-GCM implementation
notInScope: Real Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys

appservices.title: App Service
appservices.summary: Web apps and plans are Vyomi ARM records with a bounded app host, Kudu API and sandbox that serve stored content; no operating-system web server runs your code.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Web sites, serverfarms, slots, config, hostNameBindings)
Site front door at /azure-data/site/{app}/ (static content, default documents, access restrictions)
Kudu API as an ARM extension under sites/{site}/kudu/api

offline.notes: The app host serves the site's stored files and applies site configuration (default documents, access restrictions, HTTPS-only, minimum TLS). Deployment Center uses the shared CI seam; an image job really builds only if BuildKit is available. Triggered WebJobs run Python in a restricted sandbox.

nano.notes: Same host and Kudu engines in the page. Deployments use the package builder, which runs no container; there is no outbound GitHub fetch from the page.

differs: There is no runtime process for Node, .NET, Java or PHP apps: the host serves stored files and a modelled process table; programs cannot be executed
Settings such as TLS version, FTP state, Always On and CORS are stored; most are not enforced against a running workload
Slot swap exchanges config, settings and connection strings only, with no traffic routing or warm-up
Custom domains are not DNS-verified; certificates are stored with a SHA-1 of the file or issued locally and trusted by nothing
Scale up/out change recorded properties; no instances are added, quotas are a published figure per plan tier
Autoscale rules are evaluated against requests the app host actually recorded
Backups write real archives into a Blob container reachable from the simulator
Kudu runs as an ARM extension, not on a scm.azurewebsites.net host; the console interpreter covers a fixed command list
WebJobs: only triggered Python scripts execute; schedules are stored, not fired
notInScope: Microsoft-managed worker fleet and runtime stacks
TLS certificate issuance from public CAs

cognitiveservices.title: Azure AI services
cognitiveservices.summary: Accounts, deployments and quotas are Vyomi ARM records; Azure OpenAI chat, completions and embeddings are answered by one small local model, or return 503 when none is running.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.CognitiveServices accounts, deployments, commitment plans, keys)
Azure OpenAI data plane: chat/completions, completions, embeddings, Responses and Assistants (AzureOpenAI SDK)

offline.notes: The local-LLM seam starts a llama.cpp server container on demand (default model HuggingFaceTB SmolLM2-360M-Instruct Q8_0, overridable); the booster appliance path may use a larger model, which was not verified here. With no model running the data plane returns the native 503.

nano.notes: The ARM control plane, quotas and Tokens-Per-Minute bookkeeping are fully real; the inference data plane answers only while a WebLLM model is loaded in the page, otherwise 503 ServiceUnavailable.

differs: Quality is toy-grade: a small local model stands in for GPT models, so outputs do not match Azure OpenAI
Keys are deterministic simulator secrets and any non-empty bearer is accepted by the inference plane
Only the Azure OpenAI and AIServices inference plane exists; Speech, Vision, Language and Document Intelligence endpoints are not served
Responses and Assistants reject built-in tools (web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, computer_use, mcp); runs execute synchronously
Deployments are accepted only on OpenAI and AIServices kind accounts, as in Azure
Network rules are enforced on the inference plane with a declared simulated caller
notInScope: Hosted GPT, o-series and other proprietary models
Content safety models and Azure AI Foundry hosted services

common.title: Shared blades
common.summary: Blades common to every Azure service (export template, activity log, diagnostic settings, advisor, resource health, support) run on Vyomi's ARM and monitor cores over the stored resource state.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Insights diagnosticSettings and eventtypes, Microsoft.Authorization, Microsoft.Support)

offline.notes: Everything is derived from Vyomi's own ARM state and Activity log; there is no platform telemetry underneath.

nano.notes: Same cores in the page.

differs: Activity log contains only control-plane operations Vyomi recorded since boot; the caller is a fixed placeholder
Export template: ARM is built from stored properties, Bicep is a deterministic decompilation, Terraform uses the generic azapi_resource form
Advisor and Resource health come from a small fixed rule set over stored configuration
Diagnostic settings deliver to Log Analytics workspaces and storage accounts that exist in the simulator; Event Hub and partner destinations count as failed deliveries
Resource Graph 'Open query' supports only a minimal Kusto subset over the Resources and ResourceContainers tables

export_template.title: Export template
export_template.summary: Generates ARM, Bicep and Terraform text from a resource's stored properties.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions)

offline.notes: Deterministic generation; Download, Add to library, Deploy and Visualize are not simulated.

nano.notes: Same.

differs: Nested resources are exported flat
Terraform output uses azapi_resource, not azurerm_*

diagnostic_settings.title: Diagnostic settings
diagnostic_settings.summary: Settings are validated and delivered to Log Analytics workspaces and storage accounts inside the simulator.
wire: Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings ARM REST

offline.notes: Delivery appends rows to the workspace store or writes blobs.

nano.notes: Same.

differs: Only operations Vyomi engines emit produce rows
Event Hub destinations are stored, not delivered

activity_log.title: Activity log
activity_log.summary: A feed of ARM control-plane writes recorded by Vyomi since the simulation booted.
wire: Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/management/values

offline.notes: Served as Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes.

nano.notes: Same; history lasts as long as the persisted state.

differs: No platform events or sign-in activity

containerapps.title: Container Apps
containerapps.summary: Vyomi's ARM core stores Container Apps resources; on the offline appliance (Pro/Max with Docker) each active revision's image really runs as a Docker container.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.App containerApps, managedEnvironments, jobs, revisions, Dapr components)
docker logs, exec and stats surfaced through Vyomi routes (offline)

offline.notes: VYOMI_AZURE_APP_RUNTIME defaults to auto: with a Pro/Max tier and a working docker CLI the revision image is run with docker run and stopped on deactivation, stop or delete. Jobs run as one-shot containers whose exit code decides Succeeded or Failed. On Free/Lite or without Docker the service is control plane only.

tech: v86 Alpine VM (optional, off by default)
nano.notes: Control plane only by default. With in-browser VMs on and a running VM, a replica is a process started from the container's command/args inside the v86 Alpine guest; the image is never pulled. An app without command/args is reported failed to start; with no running VM runtime operations answer 409.

differs: Without the Docker runtime, replicas and revision health are bookkeeping; ingress FQDNs and traffic weights are stored and validated but no proxy routes by weight
Custom scale rules (HTTP, CPU, custom) are stored but never evaluated; min/max replicas bound the reported count
Dapr components are stored; no Dapr sidecar runs
Authentication and custom domains are configuration only; user-assigned identities are not modelled
Environment network settings are validated (subnet size, internal mode) but there is no network fabric behind them
Nano replicas share one VM with no per-container isolation and only live while the tab keeps the VM running

cosmos.title: Azure Cosmos DB
cosmos.summary: Vyomi's own Cosmos DB (Core/SQL API) core stores documents in memory-backed, persisted state and speaks the Cosmos REST wire; there is no Cosmos engine and no MongoDB/Cassandra/Gremlin API.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.DocumentDB databaseAccounts, sqlDatabases, containers, throughput)
Cosmos DB SQL (Core) REST API for databases, containers, documents and SQL queries (azure-cosmos SDK)
OData v4 feed and CSV/JSON/Parquet export (Power BI)

offline.notes: Documents are held by Vyomi's CosmosStore in the persisted Azure state slot; no external database. Parquet export uses pyarrow, which is present only on the appliance.

nano.notes: Same core with an in-memory store persisted to IndexedDB. OData, CSV and JSON exports work; Parquet export answers 501.

differs: Only the SQL (Core) API is served: no MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin or Table API wire
One data keyspace is shared by every Cosmos account in the space: a database created under one account is visible from any other
SQL query support is a subset: single logical operator per WHERE (no mixed AND/OR or parentheses), one ORDER BY field
Consistency levels, multi-region writes and failover are validated ARM state; data reads behave as a single logical region
Request-unit charges are modelled from request size, not metered by a real RU engine; throughput limits are not enforced on data copy
Change feed is latest-version mode only; deletes are not in the feed; a cosmosDBTrigger Python function runs inline on each write
Backup and restore: ARM policy and restorable-account timeline are modelled, but a restored account gets databases and containers without documents
Power BI export: real OData v4 / CSV / JSON / Parquet over container data; Parquet is offline only
Dedicated gateway cache is an in-memory per-process cache with 1000 entries per account
Customer-managed-key encryption is envelope encryption through Vyomi's Key Vault core with a keystream-XOR plus HMAC-SHA256 cipher (core/azure_cmk_core.py), not an AES-GCM implementation

cost.title: Cost Management
cost.summary: Cost views are computed by Vyomi's own cost model from the live resource inventory at real-Azure list prices; nothing is metered or billed.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.CostManagement, Microsoft.Consumption, budgets, exports, reservations, savings plans)

offline.notes: Month-to-date and run-rate come from resource creation times and a list-price table, not from usage metering.

nano.notes: Same engine in the page.

differs: Daily and monthly granularity is an even split of the month-to-date total, not per-day usage
Exports compute totals but do not deliver a CSV into a storage account
Only budget-threshold alerts exist; anomaly alerts are not generated
Reservations and savings plans are created directly with a size/commitment; the purchase checkout is not modelled
Hybrid Benefit is a flat 20% discount on the list price of a Windows Server VM
Cost allocation splits by resource group only, not by tag
One subscription; no management groups or billing accounts
notInScope: Payment methods and payment instruments (never captured)

defender.title: Defender for Cloud
defender.summary: Vyomi's own rule engine raises recommendations and alerts from stored ARM state, with real Trivy scanning of exported ARM templates and images and real Kubescape scanning of AKS objects on the offline appliance.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Security assessments, pricings, secureScores, alerts, automations)

offline.notes: DevOps security exports each resource group as an ARM template and scans it with Trivy misconfiguration in a no-network container; container image scans use Trivy when Docker and the image are present. Kubernetes recommendations run the Kubescape CLI as a sibling container (digest-pinned, no network) against objects stored in the cluster. The other panels are a rule engine over ARM state. Both scanners need Docker and a one-time database/artifact download.

tech: OPA compiled to WebAssembly (Kubescape regolibrary controls)
nano.notes: Trivy and the Kubescape CLI cannot run in a browser: DevOps security answers 501 and image scans use a bundled curated advisory snapshot. Kubernetes findings come from 22 of the 61 Kubescape controls compiled to WebAssembly and evaluated in the page.

differs: Only the Containers and Storage plans change behaviour; every other plan toggle reads back as set but enables no protection
Recommendations are Vyomi's own rule set, evaluated live over ARM state; Azure's full built-in catalogue is not reproduced, and the secure score is computed with Azure's formula over that smaller set
Alerts come from a deterministic rule engine over control-plane calls Vyomi served, not threat intelligence
Image vulnerabilities without Docker use a bundled advisory snapshot (layer tarballs are not unpacked); findings attach to the subscription's first registry
Kubescape controls that need a live control plane, node data or cloud APIs are not evaluated; Nano evaluates 22 of 61 controls
Compliance shows NSA-CISA, MITRE ATT&CK and CIS Kubernetes scores from Kubescape; Azure's regulatory standards (MCSB, PCI DSS, ISO 27001) are not simulated
Attack paths are derived from configuration, not observed activity
Workflow automation Workspace actions write a SecurityAlert row; Logic App and Event Hub actions are recorded Failed (no runtime)
notInScope: Defender threat intelligence and detection feeds
Agent-based plans (servers, SQL, App Service threat detection)

defender-storage.title: Defender for Storage
defender-storage.summary: On-upload malware scanning is Vyomi's own signature scanner (SHA-256 and literal content signatures), not an antivirus engine.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Security DefenderForStorageV2, OnUploadMalwareScanning)
Blob index tags via ?comp=tags and x-ms-tags

offline.notes: Scans blobs on upload, including members of zip files two levels deep, within a size cap, against built-in test signatures and signatures the operator registers.

nano.notes: Same scanner in the page.

differs: It detects the standard EICAR-style test strings and registered signatures; it is not a real antivirus engine and will not detect real-world malware
There is no tag-based blob query; the scan-results Event Grid topic is stored but no event is delivered
Sensitive data discovery is stored, not run
notInScope: Microsoft Defender Antivirus signatures and threat intelligence

dns.title: Azure DNS
dns.summary: Zones and record sets are stored by Vyomi's own DNS core, and an HTTP query endpoint answers lookups from them; no DNS server process was found.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Network/dnsZones, record sets of all types)
az network dns / azure-mgmt-dns

offline.notes: Zones live in the ARM state; GET /azure-data/dns/query?name=&type= answers from them in a DNS-over-HTTPS-style JSON. No CoreDNS or port 53 listener was found for Azure DNS.

nano.notes: Same core in the page for the ARM side; the HTTP query route is an appliance route and was not verified in Nano.

differs: Public and private zones are the same ARM type distinguished by zoneType; real Azure uses a separate privateDnsZones type
Alias record sets store the target but do not resolve it to the target's records
No delegation: nothing outside the simulator resolves these zones
VNet links are plain reference lists on the zone, not independent virtualNetworkLinks resources
notInScope: Azure's authoritative DNS network and anycast name servers

entra.title: Microsoft Entra ID
entra.summary: Vyomi's own Microsoft Graph core serves users, groups, app registrations and sign-ins from a directory store, and issues tokens for the password and client-credential grants.
wire: Microsoft Graph v1.0 / beta REST (users, groups, applications, servicePrincipals, domains, administrativeUnits, $batch)
OAuth2 v2.0 token and authorize endpoints (password and client credentials)

offline.notes: The directory is an in-process GraphStore persisted per space; there is no external identity provider or LDAP server.

nano.notes: Same cores and GraphStore in the page; state persists to IndexedDB. The 'unified' offline route is not needed in the browser.

differs: Dynamic group membership rules are stored but never evaluated
Domains are never verified (no DNS TXT check)
Sign-in logs record only sign-ins performed against Vyomi's token endpoint; IP address is the loopback address and no location is derived
Conditional Access is evaluated on the password grant only; Per-user MFA state blocks the password grant but there is no authenticator enrolment
Devices are registered through the API; no OS join client exists and BitLocker keys are an escrow store only
Licenses are a fixed three-SKU catalogue without billing; service-plan toggles are stored only
Admin units membership is stored; scoped role assignments over them are not enforced
Application permissions and admin consent are not an enforced workflow; only User.Read is seeded
notInScope: Real Microsoft tenant, federation and Microsoft 365 services

eventgrid.title: Event Grid
eventgrid.summary: Topics and event subscriptions are Vyomi ARM resources, and published events are matched against subscription filters and delivered by Vyomi's own delivery code.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.EventGrid topics, domains, systemTopics, eventSubscriptions, namespaces)
Event Grid topic publish endpoint (POST to the topic endpoint)

offline.notes: Destinations are Service Bus queue/topic, Storage Queue, WebHook and Azure Function. Offline, WebHook delivery to loopback and private-network targets runs in a background thread; there is no internet egress.

nano.notes: Same engine in the page; Service Bus and Storage Queue destinations deliver into the in-browser stores. WebHook delivery depends on browser fetch/CORS and was not verified.

differs: The webhook validation handshake, retry policies and advanced filters beyond a bounded operator subset are not modelled; dead-lettering is decided but not stored beyond counters
Only the topic-scoped and resource-scoped subscriptions deliver; system topics store the source but no Azure-service event is generated on its own
Storage, Key Vault, App Configuration and API Management do not emit their data-plane system events on their own; they fire from 'Send test event'
Domains, partner topics and namespaces round-trip as resources; MQTT broker, domain topics and partner workflows are not modelled
Metrics are real counters from publish and delivery activity

functionapp.title: Function App
functionapp.summary: Function apps are Vyomi ARM records whose function code runs in a restricted Python sandbox; other runtimes are not executed.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Web/sites kind=functionapp, functions, keys, host config)
HTTP trigger invoke at /azure-data/functions/{app}/{fn}
Kudu API as an ARM extension

offline.notes: Only the Python programming model with a main(req) entry point runs, in a restricted sandbox with no filesystem, network or process access and a curated standard library. The HTTP and Cosmos DB change-feed triggers execute; queue, blob, timer and Service Bus triggers never fire. Invocation is tier-flagged as needing a booster in the tier map.

nano.notes: The same sandbox in the page; no container, no outbound network.

differs: Node, .NET, Java and PowerShell functions are stored but never run
Scale settings are stored; only a configured capacity of zero is enforced (429); instances and concurrency are not modelled because invocations are synchronous
VNet integration and private endpoints are stored only; disabling public network access is enforced
Publish profile credentials are simulator-generated and grant no real deployment access
CORS checks the Origin header only; no preflight round trip
Telemetry holds the last 200 recorded invocations; Application Insights data comes from Vyomi's OTLP recorder
Authentication enforces unauthenticatedClientAction against a simulator token or a JWT with the right claims; there is no real Entra login redirect target
notInScope: Azure Functions host, scale controller and Premium/Flex instances

keyvaults.title: Key Vault
keyvaults.summary: Vyomi's own Key Vault cores serve keys, secrets and certificates over the native Key Vault REST API, with ARM-level access policies and RBAC enforced.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.KeyVault vaults, access policies, network rules)
Key Vault data plane REST for keys, secrets, certificates (azure-keyvault-* SDKs)

offline.notes: Secrets, certificates and keys are held in the space's persisted Key Vault state slot, not in HashiCorp Vault, for the v4 wire (pre-v4 Vault-held data is adopted once). When the cryptography library is importable, which it is on the appliance, RSA keys are real and the native CryptographyClient can encrypt locally.

nano.notes: Same cores with in-memory stores persisted to IndexedDB. Without the cryptography library the key operations use a symmetric authenticated envelope and HMAC-based sign/verify; round-trips are real but the ciphertext is not RSA.

differs: Nano: advertised RSA public numbers are cosmetic; encrypt/decrypt and wrap/unwrap use a symmetric envelope and sign/verify use HMAC, so output cannot be verified by an external RSA tool
Key Vault is not a hardware security module: no FIPS 140-2 HSM,
Certificate issuance is self-signed or imported PEM only; no external certificate authority integration, and GET pending always reports completed
Soft-delete retention dates are informational: nothing is purged automatically, and re-creating a deleted name overwrites it
Access policies and RBAC are evaluated for one simulated signed-in identity; access for a second distinct principal is not modelled
Network rules treat 'selected networks' as deny-everything and apply to console-tagged calls (x-vyomi-vault); calls that name no vault bypass them
Key rotation policy is not modelled; the Resource access flags (VM deployment, disk encryption, template deployment) are stored only
One Key Vault namespace per space: the vault segment in the URL is accepted but is not a partition

loganalytics.title: Log Analytics
loganalytics.summary: Workspaces, tables and saved searches are Vyomi ARM records, and Vyomi's own small KQL interpreter runs queries over rows stored in the workspace; there is no Kusto engine.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.OperationalInsights workspaces, tables, savedSearches, dataSources, linkedStorageAccounts)
ARM query pass-through POST .../workspaces/{ws}/api/query (the path the portal Logs blade uses)
HTTP Data Collector / Logs Ingestion APIs for custom tables

offline.notes: Query engine: a hand-written Python interpreter for a KQL subset (table, where, project, sort, take, count) over rows held in the workspace's persisted store; Monitor log alerts use a wider subset in azure_alerts_core (extend, summarize, top, distinct). Rows come from the Activity log (AzureActivity), diagnostic-setting delivery (AzureDiagnostics, SecurityAlert) and data ingested through the collector APIs. All other built-in tables stay empty.

nano.notes: The same interpreter and store in the page, persisted to IndexedDB.

differs: Only a KQL subset is understood; summarize, join and the rest of the language return an ARM-shaped error rather than an empty result
The api.loganalytics.io host (azure-monitor-query / LogsQueryClient) is not modelled; only the ARM pass-through is
Data sources and agents are stored but never receive data because no agent exists; shared keys are derived from the workspace id
Heartbeat, Perf, Syslog, Event and Usage tables are always empty
Data export writes JSON lines for ingested rows into blobs of the destination storage account
Private Link scopes (AMPLS) and access modes are not evaluated; ingestion/query public access is enforced with a declared simulated caller
Workbooks render Log Analytics query items from the same subset; metrics, Resource Graph and custom-endpoint items are reported unsupported
notInScope: Azure Monitor agents and Microsoft Sentinel

managedidentity.title: Managed identities
managedidentity.summary: User-assigned identities are ARM records in Vyomi's engine with minted principal, client and tenant ids that other resources can reference.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities)

offline.notes: Identity ids are generated and persisted with the ARM state; role assignments on the principal are evaluated by Vyomi's IAM core.

nano.notes: Same engine in the page.

differs: There is no token endpoint for user-assigned identities (no IMDS or federated credential exchange)
Deleting an identity does not detach it from resources that reference it
System-assigned identities on other resources mint a stable principal id; their tokens exist only through Vyomi's simulated IMDS used by VM Run command
notInScope: Real Entra token issuance for managed identities

monitor.title: Azure Monitor
monitor.summary: Alert rules, action groups, workbooks and autoscale are Vyomi ARM resources evaluated by Vyomi's own engines over metrics and logs that Vyomi itself records.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Insights metricAlerts, activityLogAlerts, actionGroups, autoscaleSettings, workbooks, dataCollectionRules; Microsoft.AlertsManagement; Microsoft.Monitor accounts; Microsoft.Dashboard grafana)
Prometheus-compatible query API /_obs/prom/api/v1 and OTLP/HTTP ingest /_obs
Jaeger query API /_obs/jaeger

offline.notes: Metrics are computed in-process: Activity-log operation counts, per-account storage counters and requests Vyomi measured; there is no external time-series database for Azure Monitor (VictoriaMetrics in the compose file is wired for the CloudWatch engine, not verified for Azure). PromQL is a hand-written evaluator (core/azure_promql.py). The telemetry recorder lives for the life of the appliance process.

nano.notes: Same engines in the page. The OTLP/request recorder lives in the open console page's memory and starts empty after a reload; fired alerts evaluate on read, not on a timer.

differs: The only platform metric is Activity operations plus real storage, Event Grid, APIM and Cosmos counters; CPU, memory and request metric catalogs of real services are not available
Alert rules are evaluated when read or when evaluate is called, not on a schedule; dynamic-threshold and availability criteria are not evaluated
Email, SMS, voice and push receivers are recorded but not delivered; webhook receivers get a real HTTP POST
Log search alerts use a KQL subset (no joins, unions, let or time-series functions) over tables that have rows
Autoscale settings are stored; evaluation exists for App Service plans only against recorded request series
Prometheus rule groups are validated and evaluated with a PromQL subset (no subqueries, histogram_quantile for rules, label_replace); remote-write is not supported
Managed Grafana is an ARM record plus a built-in dashboard; Vyomi runs no Grafana server
Data collection rules and endpoints are stored; no agent collects or routes data
SCOM managed instance and Azure Local insights are configuration only

nsgs.title: Network security groups
nsgs.summary: NSG rules are stored in Vyomi's ARM core and evaluated by the shared netsim engine; offline they can also be enforced on real container traffic with nftables.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (networkSecurityGroups, securityRules, networkWatchers flowLogs and packetCaptures)

offline.notes: Same enforcement path as virtual networks: only when VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE is on and the Docker backend runs the instances. Flow logs and packet captures are summaries derived from netsim, not a wire capture.

nano.notes: Rules are evaluated logically for IP flow verify, next hop, effective rules and connectivity checks; no packets exist to enforce on.

differs: Evaluation follows subnet NSG then NIC NSG with default rules and service tags as implemented by netsim
Packet captures are flow summaries in pcap form, not wire captures, and need no NetworkWatcherAgent
Flow logs are generated from evaluated flows, not from a physical network
Export template for this blade generates ARM only; Bicep and Terraform are not generated here

wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions)

tech: Python cores of the parent service
Docker (container task template, Parquet export via pyarrow)
offline.notes: See each sub entry for what runs and what is offline only.

nano.notes: Same cores in the page; container and Parquet features are not available.

differs: Each panel inherits the limits of its parent service; see the sub entries
notInScope: Services that exist only inside Microsoft's cloud, such as the Power BI service and Microsoft Fabric

nano.notes: Recurrence schedules fire only while the tab is open; the container template answers 501.

sql_integrations.title: SQL integrations: Fabric mirroring
sql_integrations.summary: A worker replicates SQL tables into Parquet files in the simulator's own Blob store.
wire: Microsoft.Vyomi/fabricMirrors ARM extension
POST .../databases/{db}/mirror/sync

offline.notes: Reads tables from the SQL engine, hashes rows, writes a new Parquet file only for changed tables, and keeps _status.json beside the files.

nano.notes: Answers 501: a synchronous Parquet engine is not available in the page.

differs: Runs on request, not on a change feed; whole tables are re-read to diff
notInScope: Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, Delta logs, SQL analytics endpoint

wire: Vyomi sync action on databases

offline.notes: Primary-key upsert with hub-wins or skip, optional delete propagation.

nano.notes: Same.

differs: One direction per run, no schedule, no on-premises members, no change-tracking triggers

sql_always_encrypted.title: Always Encrypted
sql_always_encrypted.summary: Column master and encryption keys are Key Vault keys; the client-side driver is emulated in the query path.
wire: Vyomi query endpoint with columnEncryptionSetting

offline.notes: The server stores ciphertext only.

nano.notes: Same.

differs: No real ODBC/JDBC driver, no secure enclaves
Cipher is an HMAC-SHA256 stream construction, not AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256

cosmos_powerbi.title: Cosmos DB Power BI export
cosmos_powerbi.summary: Real OData v4 feed plus CSV, JSON and Parquet downloads over container data.
wire: OData v4 (service document, $metadata, entity sets with $top/$skip)
CSV / JSON / Parquet downloads

offline.notes: Reads documents from the Cosmos store.

nano.notes: OData, CSV and JSON work; Parquet answers 501.

cosmos_data_migration.title: Cosmos DB data migration
cosmos_data_migration.summary: Container-to-container and JSON-to-container copy through the data-plane write path.
wire: Cosmos REST write path

offline.notes: System properties are regenerated; change feed and triggers see each row.

nano.notes: Same.

differs: No external sources (MongoDB, SQL Server, CSV from disk), no live sync, RU limits not applied

keyvault_deleted_objects.title: Key Vault deleted objects
keyvault_deleted_objects.summary: Soft-deleted keys and secrets can be listed, recovered or purged over the native REST.
wire: /deletedkeys and /deletedsecrets REST

nano.notes: Same.

Re-creating a deleted name overwrites it instead of returning 409
Deleted certificates are not modelled

entra_bitlocker.title: Entra BitLocker keys
entra_bitlocker.summary: An escrow store for recovery keys in the real recovery-password format.
wire: Microsoft Graph informationProtection/bitlocker/recoveryKeys

offline.notes: Each read is audited.

nano.notes: Same.

apim_capacity.summary: A throughput gauge computed from recorded gateway requests.

storage_private_endpoints.title: Storage private endpoint connections
storage_private_endpoints.summary: Private endpoints targeting the account write connection records that approve/reject flow back to.
wire: Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints ARM

offline.notes: No packet is routed.

nano.notes: Same.

resourcegroups.title: Resource groups
resourcegroups.summary: Resource groups, deployments and tools run on Vyomi's own ARM engine, which stores every resource in one flat map and evaluates a bounded template language.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (resourceGroups, deployments, deployment stacks, locks, moveResources, Microsoft.Authorization)

offline.notes: ARM state is space-scoped and persisted. The Tasks tab includes a 'Run a script in a container' template that runs a throw-away Docker container (no network, 256 MB, read-only filesystem, image must already exist locally).

nano.notes: Same ARM engine in the page. The container task template answers 501 because there is no container engine in the browser.

differs: Template deployments substitute literal parameters and variables and create each listed resource through the ARM dispatcher; only a subset of template functions, no linked templates
Deployment stacks own provisioned resources but do not support management-group unmanage actions or full deny-settings
Resource moves re-parent resources inside the one simulated subscription
Open query (Resource Graph) and Manage view are not simulated on this blade
Role assignments are scoped to the resource group they were created under

servicebus.title: Service Bus
servicebus.summary: Vyomi's own Service Bus core serves queues, topics and subscriptions over a Vyomi-invented REST surface backed by the shared messaging store; AMQP 1.0 in progress.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.ServiceBus namespaces, queues, topics, authorization rules)
Vyomi namespace-root REST (atom+xml entities, BrokerProperties, /messages, $deadletterqueue); stock azure-servicebus SDKs speak AMQP and cannot connect today

offline.notes: Entities and message bodies are held in the persisted Azure Service Bus state slot (no NATS or RabbitMQ in this path). AMQP 1.0 in progress: a separate branch (v4/azure-sb-amqp) is building a real AMQP data plane; it is not merged and does not work on this trunk.

nano.notes: Same REST core in the page with an in-memory store persisted to IndexedDB. AMQP 1.0 in progress; no AMQP in the browser today.

differs: Not AMQP: the azure-servicebus SDK, Service Bus Explorer tools and anything that dials port 5671/5672 cannot connect; only the Vyomi REST surface works
The REST data plane is simplified: complete, defer and dead-letter act by sequence number rather than the SDK lock-token dance; peek re-reads the same backlog
Entity names are global across every namespace in the space, so two namespaces with the same queue name share one backlog
Sessions, scheduled messages, transfer queues and forwarding are not modelled; their counts read zero
Only message TTL, lock duration and dead-lettering on expiration are enforced; maxDeliveryCount and partitioning round-trip but are not enforced
Tier gates are enforced (Basic cannot create topics or use sessions/duplicate detection); throughput and size limits per tier are not
Geo-recovery pairing and failover are ARM state; no message data moves
Network rule sets are enforced on the REST wire with a declared simulated caller; they cannot be exercised through AMQP
Customer-managed-key encryption is envelope encryption through Vyomi's Key Vault core with a keystream-XOR plus HMAC-SHA256 cipher (core/azure_cmk_core.py), not an AES-GCM implementation
notInScope: Premium messaging unit capacity and partitions

sql.title: Azure SQL
sql.summary: Vyomi's own ARM and query-over-HTTP layer runs your SQL on SQLite database files; there is no SQL Server engine and no TDS listener.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) for servers, databases, firewall rules, auditing, TDE, geo-replication, retention
HTTP query endpoint returning {columns, rows, rowCount} (the console Query editor and SDK-style clients)

offline.notes: Each database is its own SQLite file per space under the appliance state directory, so rows survive a restart. The core docstring mentions Postgres behind the SqlStore seam, but the Azure SQL store wired on the appliance (AppStateAzureSqlStore) uses SQLite files; Postgres is not used for Azure SQL.

nano.notes: Same core and SQLite engine in the browser tab; databases live in browser memory and are persisted to IndexedDB. PGlite is used in the browser for RDS and Cloud SQL, not for Azure SQL. Fabric mirroring to Parquet answers 501 here (needs pyarrow).

differs: No TDS: sqlcmd, SSMS, ODBC/JDBC and pyodbc cannot connect; queries go over HTTP
SQL dialect is SQLite's, not T-SQL: stored procedures, T-SQL-specific syntax and real SQL authentication are not modelled
Firewall, virtual network rules and private endpoints are enforced on the HTTP query path using a declared simulated caller (x-vyomi-source-ip and related headers), not a real client network
Transparent data encryption state is stored but data at rest is not encrypted; a customer-managed key protector is enforced only as a precondition for access
Backups are real table-data snapshots plus a statement log; point-in-time restore replays that log, with no replication lag and no regional placement
Query performance, auditing and watcher views are built from Vyomi's own statement timings, not Query Store or Extended Events
Export/import writes a replayable-SQL .bacpac into the simulator's own Blob store; only Vyomi-written bacpacs import
Always Encrypted uses an emulated driver and an HMAC-SHA256 stream construction, not AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256
Fabric mirroring (offline only) copies tables to Parquet in the simulator's Blob store; it runs on request, re-reads whole tables to diff, and has no change-feed tail
Sample data is a small fixed schema, not AdventureWorksLT
notInScope: Microsoft Fabric (workspaces, OneLake, Delta logs, SQL analytics endpoint)
Purview and Defender for SQL threat detection

storage.title: Azure Storage
storage.summary: Vyomi's own Blob, Queue, Table and Files cores speak the native Azure wires; offline, Blob bytes are also mirrored into Azurite.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Storage: accounts, keys, blob/file/queue/table services, replication policies)
Blob REST (azure-storage-blob SDK, az storage blob)
Queue REST (azure-storage-queue)
Table REST / OData JSON (azure-data-tables)
Microsoft.Insights metrics for the account

offline.notes: Blob containers and bytes are held in the appliance state slot and mirrored to Azurite when CLOUDLEARN_AZURITE_URL is reachable (older Azurite-only blobs are adopted lazily). Queue and Table data are held in Vyomi's own persisted state slots, not in Azurite, on the v4 wire path; a separate Azurite-backed queue store exists for the pre-v4 handler and was not verified as the live path. Azure Files are ARM records plus content kept in Vyomi's store, not an SMB/NFS server.

tech: in-memory blob, queue and table stores
nano.notes: The same cores run in the browser with in-memory stores persisted to IndexedDB. No Azurite and no SMB/NFS listener in a browser; Parquet-based features answer 501.

differs: SharedKey and SAS signatures are accepted but not verified, so a rotated key does not invalidate old requests
Only block blobs are simulated; page and append blobs are not
Only the Blob endpoint is a live URL; Data Lake, File, Queue and Table endpoints shown are cosmetic, and queues and tables use one namespace shared by all accounts in the space
Redundancy, geo-replication and failover are ARM-level state with no second physical copy; RA-GRS exposes a read-only secondary endpoint onto the same data
Soft delete, lifecycle and object replication are enforced lazily on access, not by background jobs; there is no WORM enforcement for immutability
Encryption scopes and customer-managed keys are validated but blobs are not re-encrypted per scope
Network rules, private endpoints and bypass use a declared simulated caller, not a real client network
Inventory runs on demand; static website is served at a synthetic path rather than a distinct host
Azure Files shares: quotas, tiers, snapshots and soft delete are enforced at the ARM and content level, but there is no SMB or NFS protocol
Metrics are real per-account counters for the Vyomi data plane; Storage Analytics logs and metrics are an in-memory ring, not the $logs container
notInScope: Real Defender for Storage threat intelligence (a signature scanner exists, see defender-storage)

streamanalytics.title: Stream Analytics
streamanalytics.summary: Jobs, inputs, outputs and the query are ARM resources, and on start a small Vyomi batch runner executes the query over a Blob input using an in-memory SQLite engine.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.StreamAnalytics streamingjobs, inputs, outputs, transformations)

offline.notes: On start the job loads the Blob input into an in-memory SQLite table and runs SELECT/WHERE/GROUP BY with TumblingWindow, writing line-separated JSON to the Blob output. It is a batch over what is in the container at start; it is not a streaming runtime.

nano.notes: Same runner in the page over the in-browser Blob store. No console page exists for it yet.

differs: A batch over the data present at start, then the job stays Running with no new events picked up
Event Hub and IoT Hub inputs and every non-Blob output (Cosmos DB, SQL, Power BI) fail the start with a clear error
Hopping, sliding and session windows, JOINs, reference-data joins and UDF/UDA are not supported
The query language is a parsed subset translated to SQLite, not the Stream Analytics engine
notInScope: Event Hubs / IoT Hub streaming data plane

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.summary: Vyomi models exactly one subscription on its own ARM engine, with policy, quotas, invoices and role assignments evaluated by Vyomi's own rule engines.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (subscriptions, providers, deployments, policy, Microsoft.Authorization, Microsoft.Support)

offline.notes: All blades read the same persisted ARM state. Invoices and savings are derived from the live inventory at list prices and always show amount due 0.00.

nano.notes: Same engines in the browser; state is persisted to IndexedDB.

differs: Exactly one subscription exists; renaming changes its display name
Quotas are a reduced subset of regional defaults
Policy engine supports built-in definitions by GUID with a subset of effects; deployIfNotExists, modify, append and count expressions are not evaluated
Advisor, Events and Diagnostics are derived from stored configuration and the Activity log, not platform telemetry
Invoices are simulated and marked as such; no payment methods are stored
Support requests are filed with Vyomi, not Microsoft

policies.title: Azure Policy
policies.summary: Vyomi's own policy rule engine evaluates built-in definitions by their real GUIDs over the stored ARM state.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Authorization policyDefinitions, assignments)

offline.notes: Evaluated in the appliance process over ARM state.

nano.notes: Same engine in the page.

differs: Count expressions and most template functions are not parsed
auditIfNotExists, deployIfNotExists, modify and append effects are not applied

invoices.title: Invoices and cost saved
invoices.summary: Simulated invoices and a savings view computed from the live inventory at real-Azure list prices.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (billing-style invoice endpoints)

offline.notes: Derived from resource creation times and list prices.

nano.notes: Same derivation in the page.

differs: amountDue is always 0.00; the avoided amount is shown instead

marketplace.title: Marketplace
marketplace.summary: Vyomi publishes its own SaaS-simulator offers; subscribing creates a Microsoft.SaaS/resources record.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.SaaS/resources)

offline.notes: Offers are Vyomi's, validated and stored in ARM.

nano.notes: Same.

differs: Third-party vendors' service APIs are not behind the offers

vms.title: Virtual machines
vms.summary: Vyomi's ARM core records the VM; on the offline appliance each VM is backed by a real Docker (or LXD/Multipass) Linux container, and in Nano a VM can optionally run in an in-browser v86 emulator.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Compute virtualMachines, disks, Microsoft.Network NICs, public IPs, load balancers)
SSH to the guest (offline: real sshd with the shared key; Nano: only through the local vyomi-tunnel)

offline.notes: With VYOMI_COMPUTE_BACKEND=docker (the default in the compose files) and Docker available, provision_azure_vm_runtime starts a sibling container (image vyomi/instance:ubuntu-24.04 unless overridden); otherwise it falls back to an LXD/Multipass container. Serial console, Bastion connect and guest views run through docker exec.

tech: v86 x86 emulator (optional, off by default)
nano.notes: By default a VM is an ARM record with a logical power state and nothing runs. With in-browser VMs turned on, the VM is a 32-bit Alpine Linux guest in v86 inside the tab: RAM is its disk, a background tab runs several times slower, egress is limited to CORS-allowed plain HTTP, and SSH works only through vyomi-tunnel while the tab is open.

differs: The guest is a Linux container or a 32-bit v86 Alpine VM, not a hypervisor VM; marketplace images, Windows guests and GPU sizes are not run
The size list is a curated sample of real VM sizes, not the regional catalog
Run command offline uses the real guest; in Nano it is a bounded interpreter for a fixed set of script shapes
Managed disks are ARM resources; disk bytes are not streamed anywhere
Backup recovery points capture VM configuration and disk metadata, not block-level bytes; disaster recovery is snapshot-based with RPO 0 and a region label only
Auto-shutdown is enforced lazily when the VM is read, not by a scheduler
Extensions, Update Manager schedules and hibernate/capture are not modelled; Bastion needs a Bastion host in the VNet and works offline only
Packet-level network rules apply only when netsim enforcement is on (Docker backend)
notInScope: Hypervisor, host maintenance and platform health telemetry

vnets.title: Virtual networks
vnets.summary: Vyomi's ARM networking cores store the topology and answer reachability from the shared netsim evaluator; offline, rules can also be enforced on real packets with Docker bridges and nftables.
wire: ARM REST (Microsoft.* resource provider, Azure api-versions) (Microsoft.Network virtualNetworks, subnets, peerings, privateEndpoints, bastionHosts, azureFirewalls, networkManagers)

offline.notes: With VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE=1 or auto and the Docker backend, netsim creates one Docker bridge per subnet and applies one nftables table per space from a privileged sidecar. Without it, rules are evaluated logically, not on packets.

nano.notes: Same ARM cores and evaluator in the page. Nothing is enforced on packets because a browser has no network stack to enforce on; VM traffic exists only if in-browser VMs are on.

differs: IPv4 only; IPv6 address spaces are not modelled
Peering state is always Connected, and traffic crosses only when both sides are linked (non-transitive)
Service endpoints are validated and checked by Storage, Cosmos, Service Bus and similar data planes, but traffic is not routed over them
Bastion, Firewall and DDoS plans are ARM resources with validation; there is no attack mitigation and no Bastion tunnel in Nano; firewall rules are evaluated by azure_firewall_eval, not on packets
Network Manager deployments write real peerings into member VNets; security admin rules are evaluated, not packet-enforced
Front Door / CDN is a control plane plus a caching edge simulation, not a global network
Advertised prefixes are config-only: no VPN/ExpressRoute gateway or Route Server to advertise through
notInScope: Microsoft's global backbone and anycast edge
